## Comparability Caveat

These two fiscal years are **not directly comparable on an as-originally-reported basis.** On April 1, 2024, 3M completed the tax-free spin-off of its Health Care business (Solventum Corporation), distributing 80.1% of Solventum shares to 3M shareholders [DOC-3]. As a result, "the historical results of Solventum are reported in 3M's consolidated financial statements as discontinued operations for all periods presented" [DOC-3].

This means the FY2023 revenue of **$32,681 million** originally reported in the FY2023 Form 10-K [DOC-1] includes the Health Care business, while the FY2024 figure of **$24,575 million** [DOC-2] reflects continuing operations only. Comparing those two figures directly would produce a misleading ~24.8% "decline" that is almost entirely an artifact of the spinoff, not underlying business performance.

## Correct Apples-to-Apples Calculation

The FY2024 10-K recasts the prior year on the same continuing-operations basis, presenting FY2023 revenue of **$24,610 million** [DOC-2]. Using that recast basis:

- FY2024: $24,575 million [DOC-2]
- FY2023 (recast, continuing operations): $24,610 million [DOC-2]
- Change: –$35 million
- Growth: –35 ÷ 24,610 = **–0.14%**

So on a like-for-like continuing-operations basis, 3M's revenue was essentially flat, declining approximately 0.1% year over year. (For reference only, the unadjusted headline comparison of $24,575M vs. $32,681M [DOC-1] would show roughly –24.8%, but that figure conflates the Solventum separation with operating performance and should not be used as a growth rate.)

ANSWER: Approximately –0.14% (essentially flat): $24,575M in FY2024 vs. $24,610M in FY2023 on a comparable continuing-operations basis. Note the periods are not comparable as originally reported — the FY2023 10-K figure of $32,681M included the Health Care business spun off as Solventum on April 1, 2024, which is now reported as discontinued operations; the unadjusted comparison would misleadingly show about –24.8%.
